summary: The Model Context Protocol is an open protocol that lets applications built around language models connect to outside data sources and tools. It covers how a client and a server agree on a version, discover each other's features, exchange messages over standard input and output or over web requests, expose data, prompts and tools, and ask a user for input, with an optional sign-in flow built on OAuth for web use. Its optional extensions add interactive web interfaces shown inside a conversation, and the project also runs a public registry of servers. It leaves everything about three-dimensional content, avatars, capture, rendering, physics, geographic positioning, shared worlds and portable identity credentials to other standards. A trap for standards audiences: version 2026-07-28 dropped the session handshake and protocol-level sessions, so sources describing earlier versions are out of date, and its sign-in model grants access to a server on a user's behalf rather than carrying verifiable claims about a person or agent.

coverage.note: Each request names its protocol version and a server that does not support it must answer with an error listing the versions it does support; an earlier handshake-based generation is covered by a stated compatibility table.

sources.title: Versioning and Compatibility (2026-07-28)

coverage.note: The official Registry removes illegal content, malware, spam and broken servers but says it gives no guarantee; nothing in the protocol tells a receiver what review a server or its content has had.

sources.title: MCP Registry Moderation Policy
sources.quote: The MCP Registry does not make guarantees about moderation, and consumers should assume minimal-to-no moderation.

sources.title: MCP Registry Moderation Policy

coverage.note: Servers expose tools that a language model can invoke, which is the core agent integration; the specification has no notion of a world, so acting inside a world is the missing part and what an agent acts on is whatever a server exposes. The sampling feature that let servers run agent loops is deprecated in this version.

sources.title: MCP Apps overview

coverage.note: Implementations should set request timeouts and enforce a maximum timeout; there is no bound on memory or number of calls for guest content.

sources.title: Cancellation (2026-07-28)
sources.quote: Implementations SHOULD establish timeouts for all sent requests, to prevent hung connections and resource exhaustion.

coverage.note: The Registry gives servers verified reverse-domain names and makes each published version immutable, but the project may mark a server deleted or erase its metadata, so a name is not guaranteed to resolve to the same thing forever.

coverage.note: The specification defines two standard bindings, standard input and output streams and Streamable HTTP, over one message format, and allows custom transports.

coverage.note: MCP is the general protocol that authoring servers such as those of Roblox Studio and Unreal Editor for Fortnite are built on, but it defines no world content or authoring operations itself, so the authoring interface belongs to each server built on it.

sources.title: Model Context Protocol specification
sources.quote: Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open protocol that enables seamless integration between LLM applications and external data sources and tools.

coverage.note: A server can expose data from an outside source as a resource, and a client can hold a long-lived stream that tells it when chosen resources change, so a client's copy can follow a live source. MCP has no notion of a world or of objects in one, so nothing binds a world object to the source.

sources.title: Resources (2026-07-28)
sources.quote: Resources allow servers to share data that provides context to language models, such as files, database schemas, or application-specific information.

sources.title: Subscriptions (2026-07-28)
sources.quote: subscriptions/listen opens a long-lived notification stream from the server to the client.

coverage.note: MCP connects model applications to tools and data; it defines no statement of what a person did in a world, though a server could carry one as ordinary data.

sources.quote: Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open protocol that enables seamless integration between LLM applications and external data sources and tools.

coverage.note: The Model Context Protocol connects language-model applications to tools and data, so it describes a connection, not a host that keeps places to export.
